title: Tell a trusted adult
intro: Sometimes something scary, confusing or unkind happens online. It's not your fault, and it happens to other kids too.
A trusted adult, like a parent, a teacher or someone on the school staff, wants to know and can help. Telling is the right move.
If someone online asks you to keep something secret from your parents, that's a clear sign to tell. A birthday surprise is fine, because everyone finds out in the end.

game.prompt: What do you do in each situation?

items.text: Someone you met in a game writes: "Don't tell your parents we talk"
items.explain: Being asked to keep secrets from your parents is a warning sign. Tell right away.

items.text: You can't decide what colour to make your game character
items.explain: That's your call. Pick one and have fun.

items.text: Someone online asks you to send them a photo of yourself
items.explain: Don't send photos to people online, and tell an adult you trust.

items.text: A classmate sent you a funny, friendly joke
items.explain: A friendly joke from someone you know is totally fine.

items.text: You saw a scary video and can't stop thinking about it
items.explain: Talking to a grown-up about what you saw helps you feel better.

items.text: Someone keeps sending you mean messages
items.explain: Mean messages again and again are cyberbullying. Keep a screenshot and tell an adult.

quiz.question: Who is a trusted adult?
options: A parent, teacher or adult you know who cares about you
Anyone online who says they're an adult
quiz.explain: A trusted adult is someone you know in real life who cares about you.

quiz.question: You're worried about telling because someone might be angry. What's true?
options: Telling is right, and a trusted adult will want to help
Only tell if it happened more than ten times
quiz.explain: Even if a mistake happened, a trusted adult would rather know and help.

quiz.question: What's the difference between a surprise and a secret you should tell about?
options: A surprise ends when everyone finds out; a secret from parents gets told
quiz.explain: Surprises are short and happy. When someone asks you to hide something from your parents, you tell.

summary: When something online is scary, confusing or unkind, or someone asks you to keep a secret from your parents, tell an adult you trust. It's not your fault, and telling is always the right move.
